item.text: The first full test run passes. I’m doing a second robustness pass now—especially around malformed quoting and very large decimal values—because those are the places where Python’s otherwise-good standard CSV/Decimal defaults can be subtly permissive or lossy.

import csv, io
cases = ['a,b\\n1,\"x\\n', 'a,b\\n1,\"x\"z\\n', 'a,b\\n1,x\"z\\n', 'a,b\\n1, x\\n']
for s in cases:
    try:
        print(repr(s), list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(s, newline=''), strict=True)))
    except Exception as e:

import argparse

import main

    path = Path(directory) / 'sample.csv'
    path.write_bytes(b'group,value,note\\r\\nb,0.1,\"x,y\"\\r\\na,1,\"two\\r\\nlines\"\\r\\nb,0.2,z\\r\\n')
    before = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).digest()
    output = io.StringIO()
    args = main.build_parser().parse_args([str(path), '--group-by', 'group', '--sum', 'value'])
    main.run(args, output)
    assert json.loads(output.getvalue()) == [
        {'group': 'a', 'sum_value': '1'},
        {'group': 'b', 'sum_value': '0.3'},
    ]
    assert hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).digest() == before
